articles.title: How traditional Chinese medicine is shaping Kazakhstan’s health system
articles.summary:
China has pledged to expand its health partnership with Kazakhstan by helping the Central Asian nation integrate traditional medicine directly into its national healthcare system, shifting away from simple product exports.
The Chinese embassy in Kazakhstan on Monday called for the alignment of high-level policy to enhance bilateral health cooperation for both countries’ benefit.

articles.title: As China’s AI race accelerates, ‘model fatigue’ becomes the next challenge
articles.summary:
On September 22, the global artificial intelligence landscape spun on its axis within a matter of hours.
In Beijing, Xiaomi engineers went live with an unusual broadcast, streaming the training run of their new MiMo-V2.6 model. In San Francisco, Anthropic unveiled its frontier Opus 5.5 model. About an hour later, OpenAI crashed the party with the surprise release of its GPT-6 Sol and Luna models.

articles.title: Elderly man found dead, wife hospitalised after smell reported at Hong Kong flat
articles.summary:
An elderly man was found dead and his wife was taken to hospital after authorities responded to a report of a foul smell from a flat in Hong Kong on Tuesday.
Authorities received a report at about 5.20pm from security staff at One Madison, a residential building on Castle Peak Road in Cheung Sha Wan, after an unusual odour was detected from the flat and the occupants had not been seen for some time.
Firefighters were called to the scene and forced entry into the flat.

articles.title: Greenpeace catches Hong Kong geopark ‘golden week’ visitors damaging marine life
articles.summary:
About 100 incidents of visitors catching sea cucumbers and digging up sea snails and clams were recorded at a popular spot in Hong Kong’s Unesco-listed geopark on a single day of the National Day “golden week”, a green group has found, following similar incidents last year.
The Po Pin Chau section of the High Island Geo Trail in Sai Kung was also strewn with rubbish on a separate day, Greenpeace said on Tuesday. At nearby Long Ke Beach, the group recorded nearly 90 instances of environmentally...

articles.title: French school unrest: students, teachers march on biggest day of protests
articles.summary:
Students, teachers and parents marched ⁠in cities across France on Tuesday and protesters blockaded hundreds of schools, in the biggest day of action in a wave of demonstrations demanding the government tackle understaffed and dilapidated classrooms.
In Marseille, Nantes and Lyon, the street protests began peacefully mid-morning, with the largest demonstration expected in Paris in the afternoon.
Youngsters held aloft smoke flares and placards reading “Under our schoolbooks, anger” and “Where are...

articles.title: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing
articles.summary:
Iran and Saudi Arabia are edging dangerously closer to direct conflict, analysts warn, after Riyadh resumed major air strikes on Yemen’s Tehran-allied Houthi rebels this week, ending a four-year lull.
More than 100 Saudi warplanes bombed rebel positions on Monday, enabling Yemeni government forces to retake much of the Red Sea coastal territory the Houthis seized last month. The Houthis had been aided by embedded Iranian military advisers.
Analysts expect the Houthis to retaliate by intensifying...

articles.title: Fire breaks out on rooftop of residential building in Hong Kong’s Mong Kok
articles.summary:
Firefighters are battling a rooftop blaze at a residential building in Hong Kong’s Mong Kok, with thick black smoke billowing into the sky.
The Fire Services Department received a report at about 5.20pm on Tuesday that items stored on the rooftop of the 26-storey Block B at the Shun King Building on Nelson Street had caught fire.

No casualties had been reported as of 7pm, while some residents self-evacuated the building.
Firefighters were tackling the blaze with one water jet. Strong flames and...

articles.title: Hong Kong’s Generation Y unhappiest amid housing and economic pressures, poll finds
articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s Generation Y residents – those aged 30 to 45 – are the city’s unhappiest age group, largely because of dissatisfaction with economic and housing conditions, a poll has found.
The Hong Kong Happiness Index stood at 5.87 out of 10, according to a survey of 1,039 adults conducted by HK.WeCare, an initiative under non-profit organisation Wofoo Social Enterprises.
The score remained below the passing level for a fourth consecutive year, despite an overall upward trend since 2024.

articles.title: Construction worker jailed for life for killing bus driver after smoking dispute
articles.summary:
A construction worker has been sentenced to life in prison for murdering a man who confronted him about smoking while they were waiting for a lift at a private housing estate in Hong Kong.
A High Court jury on Tuesday found Tam Yun-chiu, 52, guilty of killing Ho Lok-man after hearing that he repeatedly punched the victim in the face, knocked him to the ground and kicked his head on the podium floor of Amoy Gardens in Kowloon Bay on September 19, 2023.

articles.title: Public outcry as China nurse dies after on-duty brain bleed, but death ruled not work-related
articles.summary:
The death of a 30-year-old nurse in southwestern China from a brain haemorrhage while on duty sparked outrage after authorities refused to classify her death as work-related.
Chen Jiajia, a supervising nurse in the medical imaging department at Guizhou Maotai Hospital in Zunyi, experienced a severe headache and began vomiting while working on August 4, according to Dafeng News.
Her colleagues swiftly rushed her for emergency treatment, and she subsequently underwent a craniotomy after being...

articles.title: Hong Kong remains world’s freest economy as Switzerland overtakes Singapore
articles.summary:
Hong Kong has retained its status as the world’s freest economy in the latest annual ranking by a top Canadian think tank, although its score has declined in recent years.
Switzerland overtook Singapore to claim second place in 2026, pushing the city state down to third in the league table released by the Fraser Institute on Tuesday.
The Economic Freedom of the World report, compiled by the Vancouver-based public policy research organisation using data from 2024, ranked Hong Kong first among 165...

articles.title: Why India is getting serious about ending the Ukraine war
articles.summary:
India’s recent push to become more involved in helping end the Russia-Ukraine war comes as the costs of the conflict continue to mount for New Delhi, amid the threat of US tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy and a recent drone attack on an Indian-owned pharmaceutical plant in Ukraine.

articles.title: Germany joins France in call for China trade defences
articles.summary:
Germany and France, the European Union’s two largest economies, jointly called for tougher EU trade defences, as European and Chinese negotiators prepare for crunch talks this week under the shadow of a potential trade war.
“The open and rules-based trade system is massively affected by weaponisation of trade, systemic market-distorting practices, and global macroeconomic imbalances,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron said in an open letter. “We need urgent...

articles.title: Short trade truce can’t paper over realities of US-China relationship
articles.summary:
The recent US-China summit yielded a narrow, caution-filled outcome for bilateral trade: a two-month extension of the Kuala Lumpur trade truce, which now expires on January 10 next year. This reprieve eases fears of immediate tariff escalation and shows that head-of-state diplomacy can still curb spiralling confrontation. Yet the short timeline exposes the wide gulf separating the two sides’ priorities.

articles.title: China’s Transsion, Africa’s top phone maker, targets US$500 million Hong Kong listing
articles.summary:
Shenzhen Transsion Holdings, the maker of Africa’s bestselling phones, aims to kick off its Hong Kong share offering on Wednesday to raise up to US$500 million ahead of a targeted October 15 listing, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company, which already trades in Shanghai and has a market capitalisation of 62 billion yuan (US$9.24 billion), could offer up to 132 million offshore ordinary shares, according to approval documents from the China Securities Regulatory Commission...

articles.title: West Kowloon arts hub deficit widens to HK$998 million as operating costs rise
articles.summary:
The authority managing Hong Kong’s arts hub in West Kowloon recorded a wider deficit in the 2025-26 financial year but expects to generate more income next year by putting a residential development project out to tender.

articles.title: Mox, BOCHK, ZA Bank and Citibank apps land among Asia-Pacific’s 10 best, study says
articles.summary:
Banking apps from Mox Bank, Bank of China (Hong Kong) (BOCHK), ZA Bank and Citibank Hong Kong are among the top 10 in Asia-Pacific, according to a study exclusively previewed by the South China Morning Post.
Sia, an international consulting firm, assessed 145 banking apps in 20 markets in Europe, Asia and Australia using 100 criteria, including functionality, user experience and feedback, with each receiving a score from 0 to 100.

articles.title: Abby Choi called ex-father-in-law ‘old crook’ amid HK$72m flat row, court hears
articles.summary:
Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung called her former father-in-law an “old crook” as she accused her ex-relatives of turning her children against her when she tried sell a HK$72 million (US$9.17 million) flat, a court has heard.

articles.title: North Korea’s DMZ landmines sabotage the South’s peace push

North Korea’s laying of landmines along its heavily fortified border with the South has laid bare how misaligned the two nations have become over their de facto land boundary, after three South Korean soldiers were wounded in an explosion last month.

archive.security_status_cs: Geopolitické napětí se vyostřuje v souvislosti s americkými exportními kontrolami AI serverů a pokusy obcházet sankce přes jihovýchodní Asii. Washington mezitím stupňuje technologický a bezpečnostní tlak, včetně jaderných simulací a snah o zajištění alternativních dodávek kritických surovin, jako je wolfram a lithium.
archive.security_status_en: Geopolitical tensions are escalating amid US export controls on AI servers and sanctions evasion schemes routed through Southeast Asia. Meanwhile, Washington is stepping up technological and security pressure, including nuclear simulations and efforts to secure alternative supplies of critical minerals like tungsten and lithium.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to react to the uncovered illicit AI technology shipments to China and ongoing diplomatic maneuvers surrounding critical minerals. Attention will also focus on Asian retail data.

archive.security_status_cs: Regina v regionu Asie a Tichomoří nadále dominují ekonomické a technologické iniciativy, včetně rozšiřování těžby lithia v Číně a vědecké spolupráce mezi USA a Čínou. Geopolitické napětí zůstává pod kontrolou, přičemž pozornost investorů se soustředí na spotřebitelskou poptávku a post-brexitovou obchodní politiku Velké Británie a EU.

Geopolitical tensions remain contained, with investor focus shifting towards consumer demand and post-Brexit trade policies between the UK and the EU.

On the economic front, China is solidifying its position in critical raw materials via lithium mine expansions and tech collaboration, while Hong Kong benefits from strong holiday mainland visitor arrivals.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets will focus on the fallout from US-Japan military exercises near Taiwan and consumer demand data from China's holiday week.

archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains stable despite an escalation on the inter-Korean border, where South Korea confirmed a landmine incident caused by North Korea. Meanwhile, the EU is hardening its trade stance against China via new market-barrier proposals, even as Hong Kong expands its financial ties into Central Asia.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou diplomatickou rétoriku kolem obchodu mezi EU a Čínou a bedlivé sledování situace na korejské hranici.

archive.security_status_cs: Geopolitické napětí zůstává zvýšené v důsledku odhalení čínských špionážních aktivit a sledování představitelů Tchaj-wanu v USA.
